subsystems.name: Cryoprotectant perfusion
subsystems.role: replaces water in tissues with antifreeze-like chemicals so no ice crystals form.

subsystems.name: Controlled cooling and vitrification
subsystems.role: cools the body fast and evenly enough to pass below the glass-transition temperature without freezing.

subsystems.name: Long-term storage
subsystems.role: holds the vitrified body for decades to millennia — realistically a passive, insulated cryogenic dewar, not any 'quantum' mechanism.

subsystems.name: Rewarming system
subsystems.role: thaws the body uniformly and fast enough to avoid cracking or ice forming on the way back up.

subsystems.name: Revival and repair
subsystems.role: restores circulation, removes cryoprotectant and repairs damage accumulated during storage.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise the subject
buildSteps.detail: Metabolism is suppressed, as in induced torpor or deep hypothermia, to buy time before cooling begins.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse cryoprotectants
buildSteps.detail: The circulatory system is flushed with a cryoprotectant solution so that water in every tissue is replaced.

buildSteps.title: Cool toward vitrification
buildSteps.detail: Controlled cooling carries the body past the glass-transition temperature, ideally fast and evenly enough to avoid ice.

buildSteps.title: Store
buildSteps.detail: The vitrified body is transferred to a dewar held near liquid-nitrogen temperature, with automated top-up and alarms.

buildSteps.title: Maintain over the long term
buildSteps.detail: Storage must survive power failures, equipment ageing and institutional continuity for centuries or more.

buildSteps.title: Rewarm uniformly
buildSteps.detail: Magnetic nanoparticles or dielectric heating warm the volume from the inside out fast enough to prevent crystallisation.

buildSteps.title: Remove cryoprotectant
buildSteps.detail: The antifreeze chemicals, themselves toxic, are washed out and normal blood chemistry restored.

buildSteps.title: Revive and repair
buildSteps.detail: Circulation restarts and any injury — from ischaemia during perfusion or damage over the storage period — is repaired. No method for this exists today.

prerequisites.why: routine for cells, embryos and oocytes in IVF, and achieved in small animal organs, but not yet in human-scale organs or bodies.
the chemicals that prevent ice are themselves damaging at the concentrations a whole body would need.
magnetic nanoparticle warming has restored function to vitrified small-animal organs; scaling it to a whole body is unsolved.
torpor and deep hypothermia are induced in animals and used clinically in surgery, but hours — not years — is the current limit.
reversing ischaemic and freezing injury across a whole body is beyond any current or near-term biology.
cell lines and samples have been kept in liquid nitrogen for decades, but infrastructure continuity over millennia is untested.

pathway.milestone: vitrification routine for cells and reproductive material in medicine and research
pathway.unlocks: reliable preservation of small biological samples.

pathway.milestone: whole-organ vitrification with functional recovery, for transplantation
pathway.unlocks: a transplant organ bank and proof that a large, structured tissue can survive the round trip.

pathway.milestone: reversible whole-body biostasis in a large mammal
pathway.unlocks: the core demonstration — without it, the chamber remains a concept.

pathway.milestone: repair of storage damage and revival after very long intervals
pathway.unlocks: the claimed use case: transporting people across interstellar distances.
